podcast.body: This album, also titled "Shout," was recorded following the success of their single, but marked a return to the "old Hugo and Luigi style." Apart from one new original, "Respectable," which became their next single, the rest of the album consisted of old standards rearranged in the "Shout" style. While sometimes this approach worked, such as on "Wring-a-Ling, Let the Wedding Bells Ring" where Ronald Isley's screaming suited the Little Richard-style lyrics, it was largely unsuccessful on other tracks. Their interpretations of songs like Irving Berlin's "How Deep Is The Ocean" or "He's Got The Whole World In His Hands" did not improve either the songs or the group. "Unfortunately for the album, also titled Shout, the old Hugo and the Ouija style came out, and apart from one new Asli's original, respectable, which became their next single, the rest of the album was made up of old standards, rearranged in the Shout style."
